title.zh: 解析等离子体色散函数

summary: Evaluate the Faddeeva function and its plasma-dispersion scaling for an already dimensionless complex argument.

identity.relation: Dimensionless complex phase argument to analytic Faddeeva and plasma dispersion values
identity.definition: w(z) = exp(-z^2) erfc(-i z), Z(z) = i sqrt(pi) w(z), evaluated with scipy.special.wofz.
identity.model: Analytic Maxwellian plasma dispersion special function, without a selected thermal-speed or drift normalization
identity.geometry: No spatial geometry; pointwise complex function evaluation
identity.coordinates: Complex argument plane, with the imaginary sign preserved
identity.boundary: Finite input arguments are accepted only where both complex128 outputs remain finite and representable.
assumptions: The caller has already mapped frequency, wave number, drift and thermal speed to a dimensionless z using one explicit convention.
No dispersion root or physical mode is inferred from the function value.

inputs.name: z
inputs.description: Already normalized complex phase argument; evaluated elementwise.
inputs.shape: scalar or any nonempty array shape
inputs.constraints: All elements finite after complex128 conversion; booleans, strings and empty arrays are rejected.

outputs.name: w
outputs.shape: same as z; scalar input yields a zero-dimensional array
outputs.constraints: Finite and representable for accepted input.

outputs.name: Z
outputs.description: Plasma dispersion value i sqrt(pi) w(z).
outputs.shape: same as z; scalar input yields a zero-dimensional array
outputs.constraints: Finite and representable for accepted input.

preconditions: The caller supplies a finite, dimensionless phase argument with an explicit normalization convention.
Requested values must be representable in complex128.
supported: Pointwise real and complex arguments, including finite upper and lower half-plane values.
Scalar and array evaluation with shape preservation.
excluded: PDRK Weideman truncation-order control and its exact approximate outputs.
fluidBW method and early-return diagnostic flags.
Thermal-speed, drift or wave-number convention conversion; dispersion matrix assembly and root finding.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises ValueError for empty, boolean, string, nonnumeric or nonfinite input, or values that become nonfinite on complex128 conversion.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Raises ValueError when w or Z is not finite and representable; other unexpected SciPy execution errors propagate.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Not applicable; no iterative solve is exposed.
failure_semantics.partial_results: None; output is returned only after all elements pass validation.

provenance.lineage_summary: SciRel evaluates the analytic identity Z(z)=i*sqrt(pi)*w(z) through SciPy scipy.special.wofz. Historical rational approximations with fixed truncation orders have different numerical contracts and are not implementation dependencies.
public_references: SciPy scipy.special.wofz defining identity and Steven G. Johnson Faddeeva implementation reference
provenance.license_status: Uses NumPy and SciPy; their applicable license texts are carried with the selected distribution.

example.description: Evaluate the analytic function at the origin.
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.kinetic import evaluate_plasma_dispersion
result = evaluate_plasma_dispersion(0j)
assert result['w'] == 1
assert np.isclose(result['Z'], 1j * np.sqrt(np.pi))
example.expected: w(0)=1 and Z(0)=i sqrt(pi), with dimensionless values.

scope: Analytic origin value, complex-plane symmetry and upper-half-plane representability.
Scalar, array, dtype, no-mutation and failure semantics.
Historical bounded comparisons against pinned PDRK N=32 and fluidBW N=64 implementations, recorded in the integration evaluation.
verification.evidence_ceiling: Direct tests verify the declared SciRel calculation and failure behavior. Saved-source comparisons in docs/evaluations/2026-09-28-plasma-dispersion-integration.md establish numerical agreement only on listed finite arguments at stated tolerances; PDRK N=16 is a distinct approximation, and both source projects are outside the current qualified D1 delivery. They do not prove arbitrary-input source parity, a chosen physical normalization, dispersion-root correctness or expert scientific approval.
known_limitations: Caller-specific thermal-speed and drift definitions are not inferred or converted.
Source truncation order and diagnostic flags are not part of this standardized output.
Finite z may yield unrepresentable lower-half-plane values; SciRel rejects them.
The saved first-stage source-prose error remains in frozen evidence; SciRel documents the analytic identity.
